bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding the Civil Engineer Salary Australia

If you are searching for a **civil engineer salary Australia**, the most reliable source is the Professional Employees Award 2020, which sets minimum pay rates for engineers covered by the award. This guide explains how to convert an hourly rate to annual, fortnightly, and weekly figures, and how tax and superannuation affect your take-home pay. We also compare award rates with the National Minimum Wage so you can see the difference between a minimum-wage job and a professional engineering role.

### How to Convert Hourly Pay to Annual Pay

The standard formula for a full-time employee working 38 hours per week is:

**Annual gross pay = hourly rate × 38 hours × 52 weeks**

For example, a Level 1 graduate civil engineer with a 3-year degree earns $33.71 per hour under the award. Multiply by 38 hours and 52 weeks:

$33.71 × 38 × 52 = $66,825 per year

This assumes you work every week of the year with no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, and no allowances. If you are paid a salary, you can reverse the calculation to find your equivalent hourly rate: divide your annual salary by 1,976 (38 × 52).

### Fortnightly and Weekly Pay

Your weekly pay before tax is the hourly rate multiplied by 38 hours. For the graduate engineer:

$33.71 × 38 = $1,280.98 per week

Fortnightly pay is simply double that: $2,561.96. Many employers pay fortnightly, so knowing this figure helps with budgeting.

### National Minimum Wage vs Award Rates

The National Minimum Wage from 1 July 2026 is $26.44 per hour, or $1,004.90 per week for 38 hours. A casual employee gets $33.05 per hour including the 25 per cent casual loading. However, the Professional Employees Award sets higher rates for qualified engineers. The award minimum for a Level 1 graduate (3-year degree) is $33.71 per hour, which is 27.5 per cent above the National Minimum Wage. More experienced engineers earn significantly more:

- Level 2 experienced professional: $39.77 per hour ($78,836 per year)
- Level 3 professional: $43.46 per hour ($86,157 per year)
- Level 4 professional: $49.02 per hour ($97,173 per year)
- Level 5 experienced medical research employee: $59.05 per hour ($117,064 per year)

These rates are from the Fair Work Ombudsman’s pay guides and the Professional Employees Award. Always check the award that applies to your role, as enterprise agreements may set different rates.

### Casual Loading for Civil Engineers

If you work as a casual civil engineer, you receive a 25 per cent loading on the minimum hourly rate. For a Level 1 graduate, the casual rate is $33.71 × 1.25 = $42.14 per hour. This loading is instead of paid leave, sick leave, and other entitlements that permanent employees receive. The award also specifies penalty rates for casuals working outside ordinary hours, which are even higher.

### Tax on Your Civil Engineer Salary

For the 2026–27 financial year, the resident tax rates are:

- $0 – $18,200: nil
- $18,201 – $45,000: 15 per cent
- $45,001 – $135,000: 30 per cent
- $135,001 – $190,000: 37 per cent
- $190,001 and over: 45 per cent

Plus the Medicare levy of 2 per cent (with possible reductions for low-income earners). Using the graduate engineer example of $66,825:

- Tax on first $18,200: $0
- Tax on $18,201 to $45,000: $26,800 × 0.15 = $4,020
- Tax on $45,001 to $66,825: $21,825 × 0.30 = $6,547.50
- Total tax: $10,567.50
- Medicare levy: $66,825 × 0.02 = $1,336.50
- Total tax and Medicare: $11,904
- Net annual pay: $66,825 – $11,904 = $54,921

This is an estimate only. Your actual tax may differ if you have deductions, offsets, or a HELP debt.

### Superannuation Is Paid on Top

Employers must pay superannuation guarantee contributions of 12 per cent of your ordinary earnings, on top of your salary. For the graduate engineer earning $66,825, the employer contributes an additional $8,019 per year, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830. Super is not deducted from your pay; it is an extra payment into your super fund. You can also make voluntary contributions.

### Using the Timesheet and Other Tools

To calculate your own pay, use [the timesheet](/) on this site. Enter your base hourly rate (do not include casual loading – use the checkbox to add it). The tool will show your annual, fortnightly, and weekly figures, plus estimated tax and super. You can also browse [pay guides](/blog) for award-specific information.

### Summary

A **civil engineer salary Australia** under the Professional Employees Award starts at $66,825 per year for a Level 1 graduate (3-year degree) working 38 hours per week. This is well above the National Minimum Wage of $26.44 per hour. Casual engineers receive a 25 per cent loading. Super is paid on top at 12 per cent, and tax is calculated using the 2026–27 resident rates. Always refer to the Fair Work Ombudsman’s pay guides for the most accurate and up-to-date award rates.
